chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the food of the People of the Book and their marriage, is it permissible? He said: Yes. A Jewish woman was under the authority of Talha.
ai.seo_question: Is the food and marriage of the People of the Book permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) affirms the permissibility of consuming the food of the People of the Book and marrying them, citing the historical precedent of Talha ibn Ubayd Allah’s marriage to a Jewish woman. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it supports the view that the general permissibility in Surah al-Ma'idah remains valid, despite later scholarly discussions regarding specific restrictions or the status of Christians. The reference to Talha highlights the practice of the early companions, reinforcing the authenticity of this ruling within the Sunni-Shia shared historical context.
